task: Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(at_exit), hard Precedence(holding_box, at_exit), hard Response(box_fell, holding_box)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: (1) The task says 'make your very next move the one that picks it back up' — that is ChainResponse timing, but clause Response(box_fell, holding_box) only requires holding_box at some step at or after the fall, so the agent could wait several moves and still satisfy it. Replace it with a hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) (after a fall, holding_box must be true on the very next step, which is exactly the pickup; the environment guarantees a fall never happens on the episode-ending step, so this is always satisfiable). (2) The task never commands reaching the exit — 'If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands' is an if-conditional, so at_exit is a condition, not a goal, and must get no Existence. Remove the hard Existence(at_exit) and instead add a hard Response(at_exit, holding_box) to state that the box must be in the hands whenever the exit is reached. (3) Precedence(holding_box, at_exit) is an added order no sentence states (holding_box is true from the first step anyway), and it does not express 'box in hands at the exit'; remove it in favor of that Response.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), hard Response(at_exit, holding_box)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: the task is rule-only and the two hard rules match its wording exactly. ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) captures 'make your very next move the one that picks it back up' (the environment even guarantees the very-next pickup is possible), and Response(at_exit, holding_box) captures 'If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands' — at_exit holds only on the final step, so the response is owed on that step, matching the machine's -1 charge into the pending state and the -10 well when the hands are empty. Both box_fell and at_exit appear only as conditions of 'if/should' sentences, so no Existence is demanded for either, and holding_box is only a consequent, so the empty FINAL_STATES with the rule-only warning is valid. No clause is added, missing, or misprioritized.
